primitives.name: Grammar Rule Actions
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Grammar rules as actions** (not tokens): each MCTS action applies a grammar production — declarative bias baked into the search, reviving Todorovski & Džeroski (1997).
primitives.assumptions: The grammar captures the true syntactic structure of equations; actions correspond to valid productions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When grammar is insufficient or misaligned with target equations.

layer2.mapping: Maps symbolic derivation steps to MCTS node transitions, aligning semantic structure with search tree traversal.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of discovered equations vs. known ground truth.

primitives.name: Risk-Seeking MCTS
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Risk-seeking MCTS**: replace mean with MAX in backprop Q-updates (one good equation in a branch shouldn't be diluted by bad siblings — same philosophy as 1824's risk-seeking PG); PUCT c=10 to preserve exploration since max-backprop inflates root Q-values.
primitives.assumptions: Exploration is preserved under max-backprop; high PUCT constant ensures sufficient branching.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When uniform averaging leads to premature convergence or dilution of promising paths.

layer2.mapping: Modifies standard MCTS Q-value updates to emphasize high-value branches, improving discovery of rare but impactful solutions.
layer2.telemetry: Convergence speed and quality of final equation candidates.

primitives.name: Contrastive Dataset Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Contrastive learning for tabular data**: auxiliary task to learn dataset embeddings (which datasets are "similar" in equation structure).
primitives.assumptions: Similar datasets share underlying equation structures; embeddings capture relevant features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When datasets lack structural similarity or embedding space is poorly conditioned.

layer2.mapping: Embeds tabular data into a latent space where similarity reflects equation-form similarity, enabling transfer learning.
layer2.telemetry: Cosine similarity between embeddings and accuracy of warm-started discovery tasks.

Grammar rules act as actions in MCTS, encoding domain knowledge and constraining the search space. Risk-seeking MCTS modifies traditional backpropagation to prioritize high-quality paths, mitigating the dilution effect of poor sibling nodes. Contrastive learning enables generalization across datasets by embedding them into a shared space where structural similarities can be exploited. Supervised learning consistently outperforms reinforcement learning, suggesting that imitation of expert derivations is more efficient than trial-and-error optimization.
